newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Credit debenture yield up in secondary mkt.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Credit debenture yield up in secondary mkt.

text.p: The five-year bank debenture issued by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd in November was traded at a yield of 2.56 percent in the secondary market on Monday against a quote of 2.53 percent on Friday, traders said.
As for the five-year debenture issued by Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) in November, very few transactions were seen today, traders said.
"The closing level for the IBJ debenture yield is likely to be 1.79 percent today," a brokerage house trader said.
The IBJ debenture was traded at 1.78 percent on Friday.

The spread between the yields of the IBJ and NCB debentures widened following news in the middle of November that NCB had distributed a written statement to agricultural financial institutions saying it would continue to support the restructuring of its troubled non-bank affiliate.

NCB said on Monday that it plans to write off 40 billion yen worth of non-performing loans in the second half of this fiscal year ending on March 31, and aims to complete write-offs of its non-performing loans by the end of 1997/98 at the earliest. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +813-3432-9780
